name: Yangpu, Shanghai: Which Side Looks Better? (Pairwise)
description:
Method replication: participants compare 30 pairs of street views from Yangpu District, Shanghai, and click the one that answers "Which side looks better?". Two short questions first ask about professional background and familiarity with Shanghai. The images are not the paper's stimuli (65 Baidu street views fetched for this template, front, back or side views with the car roof cropped, 2016–2022 captures).

Original study: Zhang, Ye, Zeng & Chiaradia (2019), "A Systematic Measurement of Street Quality through Multi-Sourced Urban Data: A Human-Oriented Analysis", International Journal of Environmental Research and Public Health 16(10), 1782. Ten experts with professional backgrounds who knew Shanghai made about 50,000 comparisons of representative Baidu street views (front and back views of each site) in a desktop program; Elo ratings trained a neural network that scored the perceived design quality of every street in Yangpu, combined with density, accessibility and function mix into a street-quality classification.

Differences from the original study: (1) online and open to anyone, with background recorded instead of experts only; (2) 30 comparisons per participant instead of thousands per expert; (3) the Elo scoring, neural network and street classification are not part of the template.
author: Zhang, Ye, Zeng & Chiaradia
